question: Is the survey's curvature (the term `ollivier_curvature` and the curvature probe, both `engine.scaled_curvature`) Ollivier's curvature of an edge? Its source says so where the short cycles on an edge share no other edge (the hard-core condition) and 'elsewhere it is the same formula'. The review of 2026-11-07: +0.333 on every edge of the triangular torus, whose curvature is 0.
known_answer: Ollivier's curvature of an edge uv with no idleness: 1 less the least cost of moving the uniform measure on u's neighbours onto the uniform measure on v's, the cost of a move its graph distance; solved exactly as a linear programme (research/curvature_known_answers.ollivier)

rule: A family is exact when the probe and Ollivier's curvature agree within 1e-6 on every edge read. Each case with an expectation is a prediction, right when the family is exact as expected, or not exact as expected and, where `apart` is given, the probe less Ollivier is that number on every edge read. The criterion passes when every prediction is right; the families without an expectation are reported.
